ModuleName: Generating Text-Based Lessons: Formats, Layouts, and Content Types

Artifacts.Name: Module Topics
Artifacts.Description: Lists the topics and subtopics covered in the module, including PreseMaker's purpose, output formats, visual themes, and content types; used by learners and instructors to preview the module's scope and navigate its sections.

Artifacts.Name: Introduction to Text-Based Lesson Generation in PreseMaker
Artifacts.Description: Introduces PreseMaker as a structured content generation tool and explains what it does, why text-based lessons matter in instructional design, and what output formats it offers; used by learners as an orientation to the tool before exploring its specific features.

Artifacts.Name: Output Layouts: Accordion, Printable, WordPress, and Markdown
Artifacts.Description: Explains the four output layouts available in PreseMaker — Accordion, Printable, WordPress, and Markdown — describing how each structures and delivers lesson content for different destinations; used by learners to choose the appropriate layout for their instructional context.

Artifacts.Name: Selecting Visual Themes for HTML Output
Artifacts.Description: Covers how visual themes work in PreseMaker's HTML output, what presentational elements they control such as colors and typography, and how to access theme options; used by learners to style generated HTML lessons to suit their audience or platform.

Artifacts.Name: Content Types: Topic Overview versus Topic Detail
Artifacts.Description: Distinguishes between two content depth levels in PreseMaker — Topic Overview for concise orientation and Topic Detail for thorough, skill-building coverage — and explains when to use each; used by learners to select the appropriate content type for their instructional goals.

Artifacts.Name: Specialized Content Types: Lesson Plans, Example Problems, and Suggested Sources
Artifacts.Description: Describes three specialized content formats in PreseMaker — structured lesson plans, worked example problems, and curated suggested sources — explaining their distinct pedagogical purposes and how to generate them; used by learners to produce instructional materials beyond standard explanatory prose.
